Senses.definition: to let someone have something as a present, or to provide something for someone
examples: What did Bob give you for your birthday?
Researchers were given a £10,000 grant to continue their work.
I’ve got some old diaries that my grandmother gave me years ago.
a ring which was given to him by his mother
I didn’t steal it! Maria gave it to me!
Most people are willing to give to charity .
The situation is now desperate, so please give generously .

Senses.definition: to put something in someone’s hand
examples: Give me the letter, please.
He poured some wine into a glass and gave it to her.

Senses.definition: to allow or make it possible for someone to do something
examples: He finally gave us permission to leave.
These meetings give everyone a chance to express their opinions.
Students are given the freedom to choose their own topics.
Language gives us the ability to communicate at a much higher level than any other animal.
Women were given the vote in the early 1900s.
She was given absolute control over all recruitment decisions.
This bill will give more power to local authorities.

Senses.definition: to tell someone information or details about something, or to tell someone what they should do
examples: She gave me some information on university courses.
My secretary will be able to give you more details.
Let me give you some advice .
She certainly likes giving orders.
They were given strict instructions not to tell anyone.
Can you give me directions to the station (= tell me how to go there ) ?
He gave the following example .
You may have to give evidence in court (= tell a court about what you have seen or know to be true ) .
He gave a disturbing account of the murder.

Senses.definition: to do something by making a movement with your hand, face, body etc
examples: She gave a little frown.
Joel gave me a smile as I walked in.
He gave her a big hug.
He gave a wave of his hand.
Don’t move until I give the signal.
She picked up the envelope and gave it a shake.

Senses.definition: to make a speech, perform a piece of music etc for a group of people
examples: He’s giving a talk on early Roman pottery.
They gave one of their best performances to date.

Senses.definition: to make someone have a feeling
examples: He gave us quite a shock .
The course has given me a lot more confidence .
His job did not give him much sense of fulfilment.
Their music has given pleasure to a lot of people over the years.
Keep the noise down – you’re giving me a headache!

Senses.definition: to make someone have problems
examples: The new software has given us quite a few problems.

Senses.definition: to infect someone with the same illness that you have
examples: Don’t come too close – I don’t want you to give me your cold!
It’s very unlikely a doctor could give HIV to a patient.

Senses.definition: to organize a social event such as a party
examples: We’re giving a small party for dad’s birthday next week.

Senses.definition: to tell someone to do a job or piece of work
examples: How much homework are you given in a week?
He’s always giving us chores to do around the house.

Senses.definition: to make someone or something have a particular quality
examples: The ginger gives the dish a wonderful spicy flavour.
His grey hair gave him an air of distinction.
Its association with the movie industry has given the place a certain glamor.

Senses.definition: to pay a particular amount of money for something
examples: They say they’re not willing to give any more than they’ve already offered.
They gave us £700 for our old car.
How much will you give me for these two games?

Senses.definition: to behave towards someone in a way that shows you have a particular attitude or feeling towards them
examples: The people were expected to give their leader absolute obedience and loyalty.

Senses.definition: to officially say that someone must have a particular punishment
examples: If you don’t pay on time, you could be given a fine of up to $1,000.
The judge gave her two years in prison.

Senses.definition: to make someone think about something in a particular way
examples: I didn’t want to give him the wrong idea about the job.
The report gives us a very accurate picture of life in the inner cities.

Senses.definition: to spend some time thinking about something carefully
examples: Congress has been giving the crime bill serious consideration.
I’ll give the matter some thought and let you know my decision next week.

Senses.definition: to help someone do something
examples: Can you give me a hand?
Shall I give you a hand with that bag?

Senses.definition: to telephone someone
examples: I’ll give you a call about seven, okay?

Senses.definition: to try to do something, especially something you have not done before
examples: I’m not usually much good at this sort of game, but I’ll give it a go.

Senses.definition: to allow time for someone to do something, or for something to happen
examples: I’ve asked him to give me a couple more days to finish my essay.
Flexible working hours could give working parents more time to spend with their children.

Senses.definition: used to say that you do not think something will continue successfully for very long
examples: I give the project six months at the most before it all falls apart.

Senses.definition: to not think or worry about something at all
examples: The matter didn’t seem important, and I hardly gave it a second thought.

Senses.definition: to be willing to change what you think or do according to what else happens
examples: I think that both sides need to give a little.

Senses.definition: to state what your official decision or judgment is, for example in a game
examples: The referee has given a penalty.
The jury will be giving its verdict within the next couple of days.

Senses.definition: to decide that someone should have a particular score or mark for something that they have done
examples: She only gave me a B for my last essay.
The judges have given him top marks for this performance.

Senses.definition: if a material gives, it bends or stretches when you put pressure on it
examples: New shoes often feel tight, but the leather should give a little after a few days.

Senses.definition: if something gives, it breaks or moves away suddenly because of weight or pressure on it
examples: The branch suddenly gave beneath him.
I pushed against the door with all my might, but it still wouldn’t give.

Senses.definition: used to say that you like something much more than something else
examples: Give me good old-fashioned rock ‘n’ roll any day!

Senses.definition: used when you would like something very much
examples: I’d give my right arm for a figure like that.

Senses.definition: used to say that you do not care at all about something
examples: · I don’t give a damn what you think.

Senses.definition: used to say that you do not believe someone’s excuse or explanation
examples: Don’t give me that! I know exactly where you’ve been!

Senses.definition: to tell someone angrily that you are annoyed with them
examples: I’ll give that boy what for when I see him!

Senses.definition: to fight or argue with someone using the same amount of skill or force that they are using
examples: I don’t worry about Emma because I know she can give as good as she gets.

Senses.definition: to help other people and do things for them as well as expecting them to do things for you
examples: You have to learn to give and take in any relationship.

Senses.definition: used to say that the amount or figure that you have just mentioned is nearly correct, but not exactly
examples: It’ll be a £1,000, give or take £50 or so.

Senses.definition: used to admit that someone is right about something
examples: I was wrong to trust him, I’ll give you that.

Senses.definition: to make someone think that a particular thing is true
examples: I was given to understand that I would be offered a permanent job.

Senses.definition: to tell someone something in a clear direct way
examples: There’s no point in beating about the bush, so I’ll give it to you straight.

Senses.definition: used at the end of a formal speech to invite people to welcome a special guest
if a woman gives herself to a man, she has sex with him
to give something to someone because you do not want or need it for yourself
examples: I gave most of my books away when I left college.
Give your old clothes away to a thrift shop.

Senses.definition: to give something to someone without asking for any money, rather than selling it to them
examples: We’re giving away a free diary with tomorrow’s newspaper.
We have 1,000 CDs to give away to our readers.

Senses.definition: to show where someone is or what they are doing or thinking when they are trying to keep this a secret
examples: Don’t worry, I won’t give you away.
Sue tried to smile, but her voice gave her away.
I knew that if I moved I would give myself away.
The look on his face gave the game away (= showed something that he was trying to keep secret ) .

Senses.definition: to tell someone something that you should keep secret
examples: He gave away as little information as possible.
I don’t want to give away exactly how the system works.
I don’t want to give the game away (= give information that should be secret ) by saying too much.

Senses.definition: to lose in a game or competition by doing something badly or making mistakes
examples: We gave away two goals in the first half.
The Democrats are now in danger of giving the whole election away.

Senses.definition: to give formal permission for a woman to marry a man as part of a traditional wedding ceremony
to give something to the person it belongs to or the person who gave it to you
examples: This isn’t your money and you must give it back.
Of course you can have a look at it, as long as you give it back.
I’ll give the keys back to you tomorrow morning.
Her ex-husband refused to give her back any of her old photos and letters.

Senses.definition: to make it possible for someone to have or do something again
examples: He underwent an expensive operation to give him back his sight.
The company finally agreed to give the women their old jobs back.
This legislation will give more power back to local authorities.

Senses.definition: to finally agree to do or accept something that you had at first opposed, especially because someone has forced or persuaded you to
examples: Eventually I gave in and accepted the job on their terms.
Bob’s wife went on at him so much that eventually he gave in.
The government refused to give in to their demands.

Senses.definition: to accept that you are defeated in a game, fight, competition etc
examples: The rebels were eventually forced to give in.
We will carry on fighting to the end. We will never give in.

Senses.definition: to give a piece of work or something you have written to someone in authority
examples: You were supposed to give this work in four days ago.
Rose decided to give in her notice (= officially say she was going to leave her job ) .
All assignments must be given in to your teacher by Friday.

Senses.definition: to no longer try to stop yourself from doing something you want to do
examples: Don’t give in to the temptation to argue back.
If you feel the urge for a cigarette, try not to give in to it.

Senses.definition: if you give of yourself, your time, your money etc, you do things for other people without expecting anything in return
examples: Retired people are often willing to give of their time to help with community projects.

Senses.definition: to produce a smell, light, heat, a sound etc
examples: The wood gave off a sweet, perfumed smell as it burned.

Senses.definition: if a window, door, or building gives onto a particular place, it leads to that place or you can see that place from it
examples: the garden gate that gives onto the main road
a small balcony giving onto fields

Senses.definition: to give something to each person in a group
examples: Can you give the drinks out, please?
Students were giving out leaflets to everyone on the street.

Senses.definition: if part of your body gives out, it stops working properly or becomes much weaker
examples: Just as I approached the town, my legs finally gave out.

Senses.definition: if a supply of something gives out, there is none left
examples: My money was beginning to give out and there were no jobs to be found.
After two hours her patience gave out.

Senses.definition: to produce something such as light, heat, or a signal
examples: A gas lamp gave out a pale yellowish light.

Senses.definition: to announce something, especially officially
examples: It was given out that the government was to enter into negotiations with the rebels.

Senses.definition: to stop doing or saying something that is annoying other people
examples: I wish you lot would just give over!
Oh, give over complaining, we’re nearly there.

Senses.definition: to be used for a particular purpose
examples: The land surrounding the village was given over to vineyards.
The whole day was given over to cooking and preparing for the celebrations.

Senses.definition: to spend all your time doing something
examples: In his youth he had given himself over to pleasure.

Senses.definition: to give responsibility for or control over something to a particular person, organization etc
examples: The running of internal affairs was given over to the Chancellor.

Senses.definition: to stop doing something, especially something that you do regularly
examples: Darren has decided to give up football at the end of this season.
She gave up her job and started writing poetry.
I gave up going to the theatre when I moved out of London.
Why don’t you give up smoking?

Senses.definition: to stop trying to do something
examples: We spent half an hour looking for the keys, but eventually gave up and went home.
I give up. What’s the answer?
You shouldn’t give up so easily .
I gave up trying to persuade him to continue with his studies.
She has still not given up the search.
The ground was too hard to dig so I gave it up as a bad job (= stopped trying because success seemed unlikely ) .

Senses.definition: to allow yourself or someone else to be caught by the police or enemy soldiers
examples: The siege ended peacefully after the gunman gave himself up.
In the end, his family gave him up to the police.

Senses.definition: to use some of your time to do a particular thing
examples: I don’t mind giving up a couple of hours a week to deal with correspondence.

Senses.definition: to give something that is yours to someone else
examples: The family refused to give up any of their land.
She was put under tremendous pressure to give the baby up.
I would always give my seat up to an elderly person on the bus.

Senses.definition: to end a romantic relationship with someone, even though you do not really want to
examples: I knew deep down that I should give him up.

Senses.definition: to believe that someone is dead and stop looking for them
examples: The ship sank and the crew were given up for dead.

Senses.definition: used to ask people to applaud someone
to stop hoping that someone or something will change or improve
examples: He’d been in a coma for six months, and doctors had almost given up on him.
At that point, I hadn’t completely given up on the marriage.

Senses.definition: to allow yourself to feel an emotion completely, without trying to control it
examples: He gave himself up to despair.
